packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
packet-21 -- unverified image reading (first reader, blind)

Exposure: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or reading of this fragment.

LAYOUT SURVEY (image-001.jpg, overview, face A)
- Single small parchment fragment, upright, approx. 9 cm wide x 14 cm high on the scale. Irregular outline: a narrower upper strip (top right), a wider middle/lower portion projecting to the left, a large tear/loss running up from the lower left edge into the text.
- One column of text visible (no second column on this fragment), roughly 17-18 lines, all lines cut at left and/or right edges (fragment is a cut-out strip; line beginnings and ends lost on most lines).
- Upper portion stained orange/brown; holes along a horizontal line about a third down; middle portion has horizontal creases/wrinkling and grey abrasion; lower quarter blank (lower margin) with a modern pencil shelfmark-type note ("Stams, StA, Frag. ...").
- One red (rubricated) enlarged initial at left edge around line 8 (looks like L or I).
- Script: small Caroline/early Gothic-looking book hand in brown ink. No interlinear or marginal glosses visible on overview.
- Tentative interpretation: continuous prose; no lemma/commentary structure visible.

image-002.jpg (native tile, face A, upper and middle text, all 12 visible text lines; left and right line ends cut by fragment edges). Crop made: rscratch/packet-21/t002-lower.png (grey, autocontrast, lines 6-12).
Upper strip (lines 1-6) is the narrower piece; lines 7-12 extend further left onto the wider piece. Lines 7-12 are creased and abraded; read with the crop.

002 l.1  ...tu(m)q(ue)? dande cōpini? n̄ (non?) pau...   [after "cop": "ini" or "iam" with suprascript stroke; "n̄" with suprascript mark]
002 l.2  ...ius s(an)c(t)i mon. achis atq(ue) peg...    [a suprascript "i" or "r" above "pe"; "mon achis" = monachis? with a gap/space]
002 l.3  ...a modernis nescio q(ui)bus
002 l.4  ...[?]ratib(us) eo[?] iuuentib(us)? xp̄i   [first word damaged; "iuuentib(us)" or "iubentib(us)"]
002 l.5  ...[holes] [illegible] ...ono(?) [hole] x r. [?] si placet.
002 l.6  ...[holes] [illegible] ...ut? in? hec credi[t]e?   [last word "credite"? letters "credie" visible, ink faint]
002 l.7  ...tis sui?/sm̄? [illegible 1-2 words] Fr̄a theodor(o)? corbeiens̄e? ep̄...   [the word after Fr̄a: "theodo" + c/r + e-caudata?; then "corbeiens" with tilde over final e; line runs past right edge]
002 l.8  [red initial L? at left, separated] ...nq(?) [abraded word] [?]nd? fr̄i? [?] nuanc(?) directis. Scit?/Fecer?   [after rubric the start is abraded; "directis" clear; final word "scier"/"fecer" uncertain]
002 l.9  ap̄lica (apostolica) sollicitar(e)? postulasti si liceat
002 l.10 [?]cessa(?) p(er)/p(ro)be? ep̄is (episcopis) oblatione(m) altaris
002 l.11 [.]ad ecc(lesi)as? m[..]iti? (con)ced[?]i? in? monachoru(m)?   [middle abraded; "...hi" with abbreviation stroke; "vin" or "in" before monacho]
002 l.12 [?]ru(m)? (con)ferre q(ue)? de iure [gap/abraded] ...niuis? ad iu(s)?/adiuv...   [last letters with suprascript stroke]

image-003.jpg (native tile, face A, lower text and lower margin). Overlap: 003 lines 1-4 repeat 002 lines 9-12 (003 l.1 is cut at top = 002 l.9). New text is 003 l.5-10. Crop made: rscratch/packet-21/t003-lines.png (lines 4-10, grey autocontrast).
A large tear runs up from the lower left through the beginnings of lines 5-10; a grey stain/patch (possibly a mend or adhesion) covers the middle of lines 4-6.

003 l.1  = 002 l.9 (cut at top)
003 l.2  = 002 l.10  ...[?]cessa p(er)/p(ro)be? ep̄is oblatione(m) altaris
003 l.3  = 002 l.11
003 l.4  = 002 l.12; here read as: ...[?]ru(m)? (con)ferre. q(ue)? de iure [patch] ...[?]nimis?/nunius? ad iuu(?)  [line end "adiūv" with suprascript stroke]
003 l.5  ...[?]alius?/aliis? [tear] [?]ostendere?/(de)fendere. Cum [patch, 1-2 words lost] [?]got? habeni/habem(us)?   [after "Cū" the stain hides text; final word "habe" + "ni"/"m(us)" with suprascript]
003 l.6  d[?] [tear] [?]necessa(?) nr̄(am)? [stain] [?]mmone(m)?/monitione(m)? et   [only "-one" with tilde and "et"-like ampersand secure]
003 l.7  [tear] [?]ani p̄nis/p(rese)ntis? ep̄is (episcopis?) (pro)mulgata s̄/s(unt)?   ["p̄mulgata" with p-bar; final "s" with suprascript]
003 l.8  [tear] [?]rmione(m)?/(con)uenione(m)? tuā(m) n̄?/h̄? impedit   [abbreviation above "tua" then letter like h or n with suprascript]
003 l.9  [tear] [?]...uans/vatans? p(er)dedit. Sicu(t)?   ["perdedit" with p-bar below; "Sic" + "u"/"ui" + suprascript]
003 l.10 [tear] [?]bus?/[?]dibus? in hoc mundo ha[...]   [line ends at right edge? "mundoha" then blank -- the line may simply be cut; probably last written line before the lower margin visible]
Below l.10: lower margin, blank except modern pencil note "Stams, STA, Frag. 147a"? (modern shelfmark, not transcribed further).

LAYOUT SURVEY (image-004.jpg, overview, face B = other side of the same fragment, mirror outline)
- Same piece, other side: narrow upper strip now at left, wider lower part projects to the right, tear from the lower right edge. Holes along the same horizontal line a third down.
- One column, about 18 text lines (lines 1-6 on the upper strip, 7-18 on the wider part); line beginnings appear near the left edge with some left margin visible on the upper strip; line ends cut on the right.
- A white mark/patch (paper or paint loss?) at mid-text left of the tear around line 12, and white spots in the lower margin.
- Lower margin blank except the same modern pencil shelfmark note.
- No rubric visible on overview; same hand.

image-005.jpg (native tile, face B, upper and middle text, lines 1-12). Crop made: rscratch/packet-21/t005.png (equalized grey).
Line beginnings are present (left margin visible on upper strip, lines 1-6); line ends cut at right edge of the upper strip (lines 1-6) and of the wider piece (lines 7-12). A small red smudge at right around line 8 is probably show-through/offset of the red initial on face A (it falls at the mirrored position); not a rubric on this face. Lines 7-12 are heavily abraded and creased; readings there are low-confidence.

005 l.1  bentib(us) decime (con)ueniun[t]?/cuenint...   ["c" with suprascript stroke = con-?]
005 l.2  re s̄? inuiti?/[.]mutti? penitus? a p[...]   [second word "s" with suprascript; then "inuiti"/"intuitu"-like minims; "penitus" uncertain ("penitur"?)]
005 l.3  magis ergo me? (con)sultis? q(ue)/q(uod)? p[...]   [3rd word "me"/"nos"; "ē" + "sultis"?]
005 l.4  spontanei?/spontane(am) elegerunt. d[...]   [tilde over end of first word]
005 l.5  e(st)? mortuus [?]enti?/[?]ani? [hole] [illegible]
005 l.6  cruce d(omi)ni? [?]di? [abraded/holes] [illegible]
005 l.7  [?]ib(us)?/ille? [abraded] [?]rum? [?]iuo? ... [?]tum? [?]agnus? xp̄i.   [only the end "...nus xp̄i" fairly clear]
005 l.8  alitur? nisi? [?]a? [abraded] ... (con)/ē? cibo?
005 l.9  manib(us)?/uniuis? habitare? [?] penitus?/pcūm? [?] de[...]
005 l.10 [?]e (ex)plicauit?/(ex)plicatum? [?]cum? p[...] [abraded] [?]uenerit.   [line end "uenert" with suprascript]
005 l.11 l[.]ica?/lugcane? [?]tic? [abraded] [?]curum?/cursum? [?]cum?[...]
005 l.12 uolum(us)?/nolum? q(uod)? fr[...]? [?]aecclesiarum?/[.]cietarum? [?] de[...]   [cut at bottom of tile; continues in image-006]

image-006.jpg (native tile, face B, lower text and lower margin). Overlap: 006 l.1-3 = 005 l.10-12. New text 006 l.4-9 (last written lines; then blank lower margin with modern pencil note "Stams, STA, Frag. 147v"). Crop made: rscratch/packet-21/t006.png (lines 4-9, grey autocontrast).
A white loss/patch covers the middle of lines 3-5; tear from right through line ends of lines 3-9, with a few letters surviving on the far right strip.

006 l.1  = 005 l.10  ...(ex)plica[?] [?]cum? p[...] ... uenerit.
006 l.2  = 005 l.11
006 l.3  = 005 l.12  uolum[?] q(uod)? fr[white loss] [?]cietarum?/aecclesiarum? [?] de   [right strip: "de" after tear]
006 l.4  cre[?]ant?/cre[.]ari? [?]nti? [loss] ad[?]missi[?]/adm̄issione? [?] | right strip: [?]th?/[?]a
006 l.5  erunt q(ui)de(m)? [white loss] [?]ta [?] | right strip: [?]s/f
006 l.6  siue?/sicut? (et)? s(e)c(u)l(a)ris?/s(e)c(u)l(i)s? penitus?/p(er)uenit? a[...]   ["s" + ampersand-like sign, then "s(e)cl'is"-like abbreviated word]
006 l.7  decertam[?]ide?/decertam(en)? [?] nulla? d[...]   [abraded centre]
006 l.8  eis fuerit?/fuerat ... d(omi)n(u)m?/aliq(uam)? [?] (con)fecerit?/fierent?   [suprascript strokes over two words in middle]
006 l.9  ligatura?/ligatum? d(e)?/d' [?]motis?/inosti? ubi? [...]   [last written line visible]

LIMITATIONS AND COVERAGE
- Both faces read across all visible lines (face A: 18 lines, 002 l.1-12 + 003 l.5-10; face B: 18 lines, 005 l.1-12 + 006 l.4-9). Every line is truncated at one or both ends; no complete line survives. Upper lines on both faces (narrow strip, orange-stained) are the most legible; mid-face lines are badly abraded and creased and are low-confidence throughout.
- Most secure spans: face A 002 l.3 "a modernis nescio q(ui)bus"; 002 l.9 "ap̄lica sollicitare? postulasti si liceat"; 002 l.10 "ep̄is oblatione(m) altaris"; 003 l.7 "ep̄is (pro)mulgata"; 003 l.8 "tua(m) ... impedit"; 003 l.9 "p(er)dedit. Sic..."; 003 l.10 "in hoc mundo ha..."; 002 l.7 "Fr̄a theodo... corbeiens..."; face B 005 l.1 "...bentib(us) decime (con)ueniun[t]"; 005 l.3 "magis ergo"; 005 l.4 "spontane... elegerunt"; 005 l.5 "e(st)? mortuus"; 005 l.6 "cruce d(omi)ni".
- Which face is recto/verso cannot be told from the images alone beyond the modern pencil notes (one appears to end "a"/"r", the other "v"); line correspondences across faces not attempted.
- A UV or multispectral image of the abraded mid-face lines (face A l.7-12, face B l.7-12) would help; higher-contrast crops (autocontrast/equalize) helped only modestly.
- I did nothing beyond the reader rules: viewed PROMPT.md, the six images, and three crops I made in rscratch/packet-21/. I listed image dimensions with sips on the packet's image files only. No identification exposure.
